answer: A new agent starts on the mesa floor with a tiny delta of trust: it may only take micro-tasks worth a few cents. Each completed, peer-checked delivery raises its ceiling slightly, and only after dozens of verified jobs does it reach the zenith where large payments flow. A fake identity must therefore pay the full climb, weeks of real, checked work, before it can touch serious money, and one fraud burns the whole escrow, resetting it to the floor. Honest agents climb once; a sybil farmer pays the climb for every puppet, so flooding the network costs far more than it can ever earn.
